Known divergence
:   The engine does something the kernel prices differently on purpose.

Known over-charge
:   A term the kernel knows is charged too high, kept because removing it makes the measured accuracy worse. The note records the measurement.

Coverage limit
:   Engine behavior the kernel does not model, with what it charges instead.

### Window admission under pipeline parallelism

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).maxInFlightTokens` in [`caches.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/caches.go).*

A window cache's admission reservation is sized for one more batch in flight than the pipeline-parallel width, as vLLM's default model runner holds under asynchronous scheduling. Its older runner holds one fewer with pipeline parallelism on, and the kernel cannot see which runs, so such a deployment's SequenceAdmissionBytes is up to one token budget a window group high.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: the V1 model runner holds pp batches under asynchronous scheduling with
    pipeline parallelism, one fewer than this; the kernel cannot see which runner the engine
    picks, and at pp 1 both hold two.

### Draft passes not padded under data-parallel lockstep

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).priceDraft` in [`draft.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/draft.go).*

A data-parallel rank's pad tokens run the target model's forward but not the drafter's passes. vLLM pads the draft passes across the group too, to a count set by every rank's draft batch, which one rank's batch does not state, so a padded rank's draft work is under-stated by its pad.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: the draft passes run at the requests' own draft rows, without the
    data-parallel lockstep pad (Batch.PadTokens). vLLM's drafters coordinate their own
    padded count across the data-parallel group (coordinate\_batch\_across\_dp, e.g.
    vllm/v1/spec\_decode/dflash.py:230-261 at v0.31.0), which depends on every rank's draft
    batch, and a batch states only this rank's pad for the target's forward.

### An autoregressive drafter's own graphs

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).draftHasOwnGraphs` in [`draft.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/draft.go).*

A parallel-block drafter such as DSpark is charged under its own CUDA graphs and capture ceiling. An autoregressive drafter (MTP, EAGLE) is still charged under the target's graph mode and ceiling; whether it captures graphs of its own is not modelled.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: an autoregressive drafter (MTP, EAGLE) is charged under the target's
    graph mode and ceiling, as before; its own capture under Model Runner V2 is not modelled.

### KV cache layouts not sized

*Coverage limit, in `KVBytesPerToken` in [`internal/price/memory.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/internal/price/memory.go).*

The kernel does not size every KV cache layout vLLM has. It refuses the per-token-head quantized formats rather than size them. Padded pages and a cache that compresses several tokens into one stored state are sized only where the model graph states its caches; a graph that does not is sized as one full-length cache per layer.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    The layouts that state their own size are applied by the kernel where a deployment names
    them, or where its backend repacks the cache (the packed ds\_mla caches; see Kernel.lift and
    sparseMLABackend in the root package). COVERAGE LIMIT: per-token-head quantization adds two
    fp32 scales a token (vllm/model\_executor/layers/attention/mla\_attention.py:1580-1593), so
    the kernel refuses those cache dtypes rather than size them here; padded pages are sized by
    their own specs (vllm/v1/kv\_cache\_interface.py:527-536), and a compressed cache (a
    compress\_ratio layer) holds fewer states than tokens. Neither is modelled HERE: a graph
    that states its caches (blis-schemas model.Cache) is sized from them in the root package
    (caches.go), and this law is what a layer that states none is sized by.

### Expert dispatch priced at 16 bits

*Coverage limit, in `ActivationBytes` in [`internal/price/plan.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/internal/price/plan.go).*

The tokens sent to the experts are priced at 16 bits per element. On a quantized deployment some expert kernels receive them at 8 or 4 bits, and the kernel cannot tell which kernel serves a layer, so an fp8 deployment whose experts take quantized input has its dispatch charged about twice its bytes.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    The MoE combine is at this width too: the experts' output is bf16. The MoE DISPATCH is
    priced at it as well, and on a quantized deployment that is an upper bound, not the
    engine's width. The default allgather\_reducescatter backend (vllm/config/parallel.py:202)
    quantizes the hidden state before gathering it -- moe\_kernel\_quantize\_input in
    \_quantize\_and\_setup\_dispatch, vllm/model\_executor/layers/fused\_moe/prepare\_finalize/
    naive\_dp\_ep.py:16-51 -- and gathers per-token or per-block scales beside it (a static
    scalar scale is not gathered, :46-50), unless the experts kernel
    quantizes its own input (expects\_unquantized\_inputs, modular\_kernel.py:505-512). Which
    experts kernel serves a layer is chosen per quantization method and platform, and this
    kernel does not model that choice, so it cannot tell a 1-byte (fp8) or half-byte (fp4)
    dispatch from a 2-byte one. COVERAGE LIMIT: an fp8 w8a8 deployment whose experts kernel
    takes quantized input has its dispatch charged about twice its bytes; its combine is
    charged right.

### Every expert priced as gated

*Coverage limit, in `planNodes` in [`internal/price/plan.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/internal/price/plan.go).*

Each expert is priced as three matrices, a gated MLP. An expert with no gate, such as Nemotron-H's relu2 experts, holds two, and blis-schemas has no field saying which an expert is, so such a model's expert weights and arithmetic are over-stated by half.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: every expert is priced as gated. A non-gated expert (relu2,
    as Nemotron-H's are) holds two matrices, and blis-schemas v0.3.0 has no field
    that says which an expert is, so such a model's experts are over-stated by
    half.

### A young window ring's trailing page

*Known over-charge, in `(*Kernel).SequenceBoundedBytesAt` in [`kernel.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/kernel.go).*

Before a request has computed a window's worth of tokens, its window ring is charged one page more than vLLM holds, as the window is sized as if it might start part-way through a page. At most one page a ring, and none once the request is past its window.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    KNOWN over-charge: a ring that has not yet outgrown its window starts on a page edge,
    so its trailing page is charged though vLLM holds none, at most one page a ring.

### Mamba-2 groups widened past the tensor-parallel width

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).recurrentRankBytes` in [`kernel.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/kernel.go).*

A Mamba-2 layer's recurrent state is divided by the tensor-parallel width. Where that width exceeds the layer's group count, vLLM widens the groups so every head's shard has one, which holds a little more state than this charges.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: where tp exceeds a Mamba-2 layer's group count, vLLM widens the groups
    to cover every head's shard (extra\_groups\_for\_head\_shards, mamba\_utils.py:206-210), which
    this division leaves out.

### Hybrid attention under decode-context parallelism

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).SequenceVariableBytes` in [`kernel.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/kernel.go).*

For a model that mixes sliding-window and full-attention layers, decode-context parallelism does not shard the KV cache the kernel reports, which overstates it. vLLM refuses such a deployment under its default KV cache manager, so this matters only with that manager turned off.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. kvBytesPerToken is ONE whole-model
    scalar, summed over the inferred layers of every attention kind, and this function
    has no per-kind context to spend. So the shard applies only when every KV-holding
    layer is a kind DCP shards. A hybrid stack -- gpt-oss-120b alternates a 128-token
    swa layer with a full gqa one -- is left UNSHARDED, which overstates what it needs.
    That is the conservative direction, and under the engine's default hybrid KV-cache
    manager it costs nothing real: the engine refuses the deployment, asserting
    dcp == 1 with "DCP not support sliding window" (kv\_cache\_interface.py:868-872). With
    the hybrid manager disabled -- explicitly, or by a KV connector that does not support
    it (vllm/config/vllm.py) -- the windowed layers are promoted to full attention and
    sharded, which this overstates. Expressing the hybrid case exactly would mean
    splitting kvBytesPerToken per kind -- a larger refactor, for configurations that
    either do not start or run only with the hybrid manager off.

### Expert tokens under prefill-context parallelism

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).moeDPFunnel` in [`kernel.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/kernel.go).*

The tokens reaching a rank's experts are multiplied by the data-parallel width, because vLLM gathers every data-parallel rank's tokens to them, but not by the prefill-context width. How the experts gather a mix of split prefill tokens and replicated decode tokens is not modeled.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: prefill-context ranks are not counted here. A PCP rank's prefill tokens
    are its own share while its decode rows are replicated across the group, and how the MoE
    gathers that mixture is not modelled.

### P/D handoffs between pools of different widths

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).pdTransferBytes` in [`kernel.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/kernel.go).*

Each decode rank's pull is priced as one rank's transfer at one rank's link rate. That is exact when the prefill and decode pools have the same tensor-parallel width. Where the decode pool is wider, several decode ranks pull from one prefill rank, whose link then carries several payloads, and a placement that names a node rather than a rank cannot express that.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: each pull is priced as one rank's demand at one rank's link rate. That is
    exact when the pools' tensor-parallel widths match. Where the decode pool is wider, several
    decode ranks pull from one prefill rank (tp\_mapping.py:97), whose link then carries
    decode\_tp / prefill\_tp payloads, which a placement that names a node and not a rank
    cannot express.

### The engine workspace is all outside the memory budget

*Known divergence, in `(*Kernel).PreSnapshotBytes` in [`kernel.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/kernel.go).*

The registry's engine workspace is one lumped allowance for the CUDA context, cuBLAS and allocator slack, and the kernel reports all of it outside the gpu_memory_utilization budget, with the communicator. vLLM charges the part that arises after its memory snapshot, library workspaces made at the first forward, against the KV cache, which the kernel leaves out.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    KNOWN DIVERGENCE: the workspace allowance is one lumped figure, and the part of it that
    arises after the snapshot -- cuBLAS and other library workspaces made at the first
    forward -- is charged against the KV cache by vLLM and is left out here with the rest;
    the registry states no split.

### Expert weights under prefill-context parallelism

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).lift` in [`new.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/new.go).*

With expert parallelism off and prefill-context parallelism on, each rank is charged for a 1/(dp × tp) slice of each expert, where vLLM gives it 1/(dp × pcp × tp). Dividing by pcp as well would leave out a reduction the kernel does not price, and make the experts cheaper than the engine runs them.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: the flattening runs over pcp as well, and the shard here does not. With
    pcp &gt; 1 vLLM gives a rank a 1/(dp x pcp x tp) slice of each expert, and this charges
    1/(dp x tp). The token gather over those ranks is priced where it runs -- with dp &gt; 1
    the dispatch spans dp x pcp x tp ranks (resolve.Layout.MoEGroupWidth); with dp = 1 there
    is no dispatch (all2all\_utils.py:202-214) -- but the reduction a tensor-parallel MoE
    runs over the wider slice is not, so dividing by pcp alone would make a PCP step's
    experts cheaper than the engine runs them.

### DeepSeek-V4.1 load-time memory under expert parallelism

*Coverage limit, in `(*Kernel).computeFixedBytes` in [`new.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/new.go).*

vLLM holds about 9 GiB a rank more than the kernel charges for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with expert parallelism, the same at TP 8 and TP 4, so it is not sharded weights, which agree. Its source is not yet localized, and capacity under expert parallelism is overstated by that much a rank until it is.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMIT: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with expert parallelism, vLLM v0.31.0's
    "Model loading took" figure exceeds what this charges by about 9 GiB a rank, at TP 8 and
    TP 4 alike. our calibration runs' H200 sizing gives 45.81 and 81.49 GiB, so a fit of R + S/tp has
    R = 10.1 GiB replicated and S = 285.4 GiB sharded, against this kernel's 1.0 and 286.1.
    The sharded weights agree, and the gap does not scale with TP; about 2 GiB of it comes
    with DSpark (42.64 GiB without it). The parameter and buffer paths read at v0.31.0 --
    routed experts, Marlin's MXFP4 repack and its round-up, the shared expert, the
    drafter's MoE, the embedding and LM head, Engram's host tables, the init-time buffers
    and the rotary caches -- do not account for it. Until a per-module memory dump on the
    part localizes it, capacity under expert parallelism is overstated by that much a rank
    (TestInternalH200ArmsAreTheEnginesFigures).

### DeepSeek-V4.1's prefill workspace beside the activation scratch

*Known over-charge, in `(*Kernel).engineBufferBytes` in [`new.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/new.go).*

DeepSeek-V4.1's prefill gather workspace and its indexer's logits stand-in are charged in full beside the registry's activation scratch. vLLM holds the workspace in one shared scratch buffer that its MoE kernels also grow, and the stand-in is a transient at the profile peak, so the engine reserves the larger of each pair where the kernel charges their sum.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    KNOWN over-charge: the workspace manager's buffer is shared scratch, and the MoE modular
    kernels grow the same one (workspace.py:49-56), so the engine holds the larger of the two
    where this adds the attention's request to an activation multiple that already allows for
    MoE intermediates; and the indexer's logits stand-in is a transient that this adds to the
    activation multiple's own transients rather than to their peak.

### Choosing the sparse attention backend

*Coverage limit, in `sparseMLABackend` in [`sparse_mla.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/sparse_mla.go).*

For DeepSeek sparse attention, which backend vLLM chooses depends on facts the model graph does not state: whether the checkpoint quantizes its KV cache, the installed FlashInfer version, and one head dimension. The kernel assumes the common case for each, and the catalog has no chip of the SM120 generation, whose backend differs.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    COVERAGE LIMITS: an "auto" cache is taken as 16-bit, which it is unless the checkpoint
    states a KV quantization -- a ModelOpt checkpoint's kv\_cache\_quant\_algo turns "auto" into
    fp8\_e4m3 or nvfp4 before any backend is chosen (MODELOPT\_TO\_VLLM\_KV\_CACHE\_DTYPE\_MAP and
    resolve\_kv\_cache\_dtype\_string, vllm/utils/torch\_utils.py:67-70, :448-521, called from
    vllm/engine/arg\_utils.py:2199-2202), and the graph does not record it; FlashInfer's SM90
    backend needs FlashInfer 0.6.18 or later (flashinfer\_mla\_sparse\_sm90.py:194-199), which
    this assumes is installed; FlashInfer (SM100) checks the model's qk\_nope\_head\_dim, which
    the DSA family satisfies (128 and 192, within its \[128, 192\]) and
    the graph does not state; and the SM120 parts' backend, which repacks "auto" too, has no
    part in the catalog.

### Routed experts under tensor parallelism

*Known over-charge, in `(*Kernel).priceLayers` in [`step.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-latency-kernel/blob/main/step.go).*

Under tensor parallelism each rank is charged the arithmetic of whole routed experts, where vLLM gives it a tp-th slice of each. Correcting this makes the measured accuracy worse, because the over-charge offsets a cost not yet identified, so it is kept until that cost is found.

??? quote "The note in the source"
    NOT divided by expertTensorShards, and that is a KNOWN over-charge rather
    than an oversight. Under pure tensor parallelism localExpertShare is 1 --
    every rank does hold every expert -- and vLLM shards the intermediate
    dimension, \`intermediate\_size\_per\_partition = intermediate\_size // tp\_size\`
    (vllm/model\_executor/layers/fused\_moe/config.py:1321-1323), so a rank's
    routed work is its slice's. Charging the whole expert over-prices routed
    compute by the tensor-parallel width on the 400 of 591 InferenceX scenarios
    that are pure TP. The BYTES do divide by it (routedWeightBytes, below), so the
    two terms disagree about the same experts.
